title: Step 14: sharp positive-branch fork (Faber-Krahn base pinning + chi-uniformity)

A_cz_determinant_invariance.ansatz: f1 = log sin x + u, f2 = log sin y - u
A_cz_determinant_invariance.conclusion: The opposite warping cancels in the determinant: w = sin x * sin y independent of u. The CZ spike concentrates curvature at FIXED 4-volume and cannot shrink volume. A volume-breaking sequence needs small p AND q, which is a genuinely different and harder construction.

B_faber_krahn_base_area.caveat: Faber-Krahn as stated is for domains with the ambient (or given) metric g_B. For a curved orbit metric, the sharp constant may differ, but the qualitative conclusion Area(Omega) >= c(delta) > 0 holds whenever a Faber-Krahn-type inequality (lambda_1 * Area >= c) is available; a genuinely singular/cusped orbit metric would need separate control. The absolute base-area lower bound is the KEY new lever: the orbit space cannot shrink, so any invariant collapse is purely fiber-side (all fixed 2-spheres thinning at once).

C_corner_pinning.corner_local_model: R^4 fixed point: g_B = ds1^2+ds2^2, w = s1*s2 (unit rise both directions)
C_corner_pinning.interpretation: int_{corner ball radius R} w ~ R^4/4. A corner contributes negligible 4-volume only if its two adjacent edges are short. Volume collapse requires EVERY corner to have a short adjacent edge simultaneously.
C_corner_pinning.dichotomy: With Area(Omega) >= A_base(delta) (base does not shrink) and the corner rise rate fixed by unit closure, invariant volume collapse forces all fixed 2-spheres (rod areas) to shrink together. The 2D question: can lambda_1 <= 2(1+delta) + unit closure + corner Gauss-Bonnet int K_B = 2pi - (pi/2)m prevent every corner from having a short adjacent edge, UNIFORMLY in m=chi?

proposition_A_chain: universal cover M~ has same pinching, Vol(M~) >= v0 (if v0 is a uniform gap)
Cheeger-Naber finite type: chi(M~) <= X(delta0, v0)
so |pi_1(M)| <= X, and Vol(M) = Vol(M~)/|pi_1(M)| >= v0/X
D_chi_uniformity_for_proposition_A.circularity_if_chi_dependent: If the invariant/simply-connected gap is only v0(chi) with v0(chi) -> 0 as chi -> infty, then Cheeger-Naber gives chi(M~) <= X(delta0, v0(chi(M~))), an implicit inequality that does NOT bound chi(M~) (larger chi allows smaller v0 allows larger chi). A per-topology gap therefore does NOT power Proposition A.
D_chi_uniformity_for_proposition_A.requirement: Proposition A needs a chi-UNIFORM simply connected volume gap v0 > 0. This is exactly the tail-dichotomy regime: #_k(S^2 x S^2) has chi = 2k+2 (quasitoric), and the energy budget permits ~chi bubbles, so nothing in the energy forbids collapse as chi -> infty. The toric route and the Step 8-9 tail dichotomy are the SAME wall.

The genuinely new lever is the UNWEIGHTED spectral bound lambda_1 <= 2(1+delta) => Faber-Krahn => Area(Omega) >= c(delta) > 0.
